2607.24190.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim
2607.24190.paper_summary: Social robots that rely on large language models for conversation are unable to retain information across sessions. This absence of memory violates social expectations, potentially preventing the formation of persistent relationships. This paper presents a lightweight episodic memory module that integrates vector-based semantic retrieval with an LLM-controlled dialog system, deployed on the humanoid robot head Kim. The module employs a hybrid scoring function combining cosine similarity with a memory strength metric to retrieve contextually relevant past interactions and inject them into the generation prompt. The system was evaluated in a within-subjects video-based online study (N = 43) using the Human-Robot Interaction Evaluation Scale (HRIES). Results show that episodic memory significantly increased perceived sociability (d = 0.60, p < .001), with the strongest effects on perceived trustworthiness (d = 0.62) and warmth (d = 0.56). Perceived disturbance remained unchanged (d = 0.00), indicating that the implemented approach to personalized recall did not trigger privacy-related discomfort or uncanny valley effects. These findings suggest that episodic memory serves as a social lubricant in embodied Human-Robot Interaction, enhancing relational quality without eliciting negative affective responses.
2607.24190.paper_summary_zh: 社交機器人依賴大型語言模型進行對話，但無法在不同會話之間保留信息。這種缺乏記憶違反了社交期望，可能阻礙持久關係的形成。本文提出了一種輕量級的情節記憶模塊，該模塊將基於向量的語義檢索與LLM控制的對話系統集成，並部署在類人機器人頭部Kim上。該模塊採用一種混合評分函數，將餘弦相似度與記憶強度指標結合，以檢索上下文相關的過去互動並將其注入生成提示中。系統在一項基於視頻的在線研究中進行評估（N = 43），使用人機互動評估量表（HRIES）。結果顯示，情節記憶顯著提高了感知的社交性（d = 0.60，p < .001），對感知的可信度（d = 0.62）和溫暖感（d = 0.56）影響最為明顯。感知的干擾保持不變（d = 0.00），這表明所實施的個性化回憶方法並未引發與隱私相關的不適或怪異谷效應。這些發現表明，情節記憶在具身的人機互動中作為社交潤滑劑，提升了關係質量而不引發負面情感反應。
